title: time-decoupled-prefetch-tiler-and-heatmap-compactifier-for-mixed-sequence-benchmarks
author: Avery Chen
body: Motivation: mixed-length conversational workloads amplify inefficiencies in prefetch and batching: short requests stall while long ones dominate GPU occupancy. This PR introduces a time-decoupled prefetch orchestrator (decoupled_prefetch_tiler) that separates prefetch pacing from token production to improve occupancy without increasing tail latency, and a heatmap compactifier reporter that compresses per-epoch occupancy/latency heatmaps into space-efficient summaries suitable for long retention. Key goals: reduce p95/p99 for mixed-seq load, provide compact traces for long-running experiments, and make kernel-level sampling cheap enough to run in nightly regression packs. Work included: a Python runner (bench/runners/decoupled_prefetch_tiler.py) implementing a time-aware tiler that schedules prefetch windows based on sequence-length histograms and observed KV-cache hit ratios; a Rust microprobe (bench/probes/kernel_sampler.rs) that emits an inexpensive kernel hotpath sample once every Nms; a Go reporter (bench/reporters/heatmap_compactifier.go) that consumes raw heatmaps and outputs compressed epoch summaries (proto-compatible with existing dashboards). The change also adds deterministic unit/integration tests, CI bench smoke steps, and a docs page with tuning guidance. Summary of results: on our mixed-chat synthetic workload (40% short <64 tokens, 40% medium 64-512, 20% long >512) running on an A100-like baseline, the tiler achieved a 12% reduction in p95 tokens-per-second tail variance and a 7% improvement in aggregate throughput at equivalent p99 latency budget. The compactifier reduces stored heatmap size by ~6x versus naive epoch dumps in a 30-day retention scenario. Implementation notes: the tiler exposes a small config surface (target_prefetch_ms, max_prefetch_batch, seq_bucket_weights) and is designed to be a best-effort scheduler — it will never prefetch more than configured per-request prefatch budget and falls back to legacy continuous prefetch when disabled. The kernel sampler is opt-in and tuned for low overhead; in our tests it adds <0.2% CPU overhead and <1% added latency variance. Backwards compatibility: reporters emit a compatibility wrapper so existing dashboard ingestion continues to work. Testing & CI: added unit tests for bucket weighting, end-to-end harness under bench-ci with deterministic seeds, and a perf-smoke pipeline that validates no regression on stable workloads. See commits and files changed for details.
commits: Initial implementation of decoupled prefetch tiler (python runner) - adds scheduling, histogram bucketing and adaptive pacing
Add Rust kernel sampler microprobe and FFI glue for low-overhead sampling
Heatmap compactifier (Go) with proto serialization and decoder library
Tests: deterministic harness, unit tests for bucket weights, integration test against synthetic-mix profile
Docs: tuning guide, example configs, dashboard mapping
Fix: race condition in prefetch lease counter found during integration runs
CI: add bench-ci step and perf-smoke workflow, adjust timeouts
review_comments: Marco Silva: Nice separation of concerns, high-level design looks good. Two asks: (1) please add a deterministic random seed to the tiler tests so CI does not flake; (2) add a small integration metric that asserts compactifier output size reduction to catch regressions.
Avery Chen: Addressed both in latest commits — added SEED env override and an assert in the compactifier smoke test. Also included a short note in docs about nondeterministic probes.
Priya Nair: Can we expose a safety cap for prefetch memory to avoid OOMs on constrained nodes? Suggest adding max_prefetch_memory_mb config and aborting prefetch when exceeded.
Avery Chen: Added max_prefetch_memory_mb with a sane default (256MB) and tests that simulate constrained nodes. Also added metrics for prefetch memory usage to the reporter mapping.
Liam O'Connor: Comments on Rust probe: please document semantically what gets sampled and add a microbenchmark for overhead. Otherwise LGTM.
Avery Chen: Added microbenchmark and extended doc comments in kernel_sampler.rs. Marking as ready for merge after CI.
merge_outcome: merged by squash (squash and merge) - commit message: feat(bench): time-decoupled prefetch tiler + heatmap compactifier
release_notes: Introduce decoupled prefetch tiler runner to improve GPU occupancy for mixed-length workloads; configurable via bench examples.
Add heatmap compactifier reporter to compress and retain occupancy/latency heatmaps with lower storage cost.
Introduce low-overhead kernel sampler microprobe for nightly kernel hotpath sampling.
No breaking changes; dashboards remain compatible via wrapper schema.
notes_for_qa: QA checklist: (1) run bench/examples/mixed_seq_config.yaml against a small cluster with deterministic seed SEED=42; (2) verify compactifier output size reduced by ~6x compared to raw epoch dump; (3) exercise max_prefetch_memory_mb by lowering to 32MB and confirming prefetch abides by cap; (4) enable kernel sampler and run microbenchmark to confirm overhead <1%.
related_work: This draws on ideas from the session-prefetch literature and prior internal experiments (ENG-3412 adaptive-kv-prefetch). The tiler differs by decoupling prefetch scheduling from immediate token emission and by operating on histogram-derived windows rather than per-request heuristics.
